references.text: Earlier in the Gospel of Luke, Jesus gives a similar exhortation not to worry about what to say when brought before authorities: "When they bring you into the synagogues and before rulers and authorities, do not be anxious about how or what you should answer or what you should say. For the Holy Spirit will teach you in that very hour what you ought to say" ([ref:Luk 12:11-12|Luke 12:11-12]).

Jesus tells his disciples in the mission discourse that when they are handed over, they should not worry about how or what they should speak, for it will be given them in that hour what they should say. It is not they who speak, but the Spirit of the Father speaking through them ([ref:Matt 10:19-20|Matthew 10:19-20]).

Mark's parallel to Luke 21:14: "When they bring you in and hand you over, do not be anxious beforehand about what you should say. But whatever is given you in that hour, speak it" ([ref:Mark 13:11|Mark 13:11]).

God says to Moses: "Go now! I will be with your mouth and teach you what you should say." God promises to give words to those called to speak on his behalf, which is the background for Jesus' exhortation not to prepare defense speeches in advance ([ref:2 Mos 4:12|Exodus 4:12]).

Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, defends himself before the Council without preparation and speaks with boldness—an fulfillment of Jesus' promise that his disciples need not prepare defense speeches ([ref:Apg 4:8-12|Acts 4:8-12]).

"The plans of the heart belong to man, but the answer of the tongue is from the Lord." This wisdom saying emphasizes that it is God who gives the right words—a background for Jesus' call not to prepare a defense in advance ([ref:Ordsp 16:1|Proverbs 16:1]).

The following verse explains the basis for the exhortation in verse 14: Jesus himself will give his disciples mouth and wisdom that no opponent can withstand or contradict ([ref:Luk 21:15|Luke 21:15]).

Paul exhorts the Philippians not to be anxious about anything, but in everything to present their requests to God. This attitude of trust instead of anxious preparation reflects Jesus' exhortation in [ref:Luk 21:14|Luke 21:14] ([ref:Fil 4:6|Philippians 4:6]).
